title: July 2026 Facebook search and source audit — social-source ledger

parentPost.author: Christine Wonsley
parentPost.visibleText: This is our Nolan Wells aka Nono. One of the sweetest and kindest souls you could ever meet. He went missing on Horn Island on July 4th. I’m looking for any pics or videos that was taken on the Northwest tip of Horn. Please help us find our sonshine.

scopeNote: The audit covers the exposed comments and selected reply threads on Christine Wonsley’s July 5 appeal, a United Cajun Navy reel, Will Polston’s active-search reel, the SMCC Athletics appeal, and Anna C. Moore’s July 7 clarification. It separately preserves three supplemental source sets: the Boogie LowDown post and four attachments, the Natalya King post and five attachments, and a supplied complete Katelynn Brochard reply frame plus four images from a public derivative repost. Those supplemental sources’ full comment trees were not audited. It is not a forensic export: Facebook displayed higher totals than it exposed in some threads, and direct July 2026 Jackson County Sheriff’s Office and Mississippi NAACP post permalinks were not recovered. Visible Facebook post and message times authenticate only what the interface displays, not sender identity, media capture, completeness, delivery, police receipt, or the time and truth of a described event.

records.message: The photos from that night alone says alot.
records.assessment: A screenshot of Christine Wonsley’s separate post showing several July 4 group photographs. The comment’s interpretation is not evidence; the underlying photos remain useful media records whose exact capture times are not authenticated.

The screenshot attributes to Matthew Lamp that one passenger was pretty certain Nolan was part of a group that was almost fighting around 5 PM, that a blue-top Bertram left shortly afterward and fast, and that three people on Lamp’s boat said the dispute was among the group. This is Lamp relaying unnamed passengers, not Lamp claiming a personal sighting. The exact event time, vessel, participants, original thread, and passenger statements remain unverified.

records.message: Friends state that Nolan was last seen around 3:00 p.m. on Saturday, July 4. United Cajun Navy Incident Commander Josh Gill reported that witnesses last noted Nolan ‘hanging out with a girl’ on the island. The waters there are notorious for being dangerous to swim in. Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter announced that a body was discovered on Horn Island. While officials are on the scene, they have not yet publicly confirmed the identity of the person found. Nolan's mother, Christine Wonsley, publicly confirmed via social media that she has personally spoken with the girl to gather details about her son's final known moments. The conversation shed light on the logistical confusion that occurred on the island. The girl reportedly stated that there was a massive misunderstanding regarding Nolan's transportation—where different factions of acquaintances mistakenly believed he had secured a boat ride back to the mainland with someone else.
records.status: Relevant narrative record; not independent evidence
records.assessment: This comment compiles claims already attributed to friends, Josh Gill, Sheriff Ledbetter, Christine Wonsley, and an unnamed girl. It is useful for documenting how the public narrative was being summarized by the morning of July 6, but it is not firsthand and does not independently corroborate any of those claims.

records.message: HE ABSOLUTELY KNEW HOW TO SWIM THAT HAS ALREADY BEEN STATED AND HE DO LIFEGUARD DURING THE SUMMERS
records.assessment: The reply states that Nolan knew how to swim and worked as a lifeguard during summers. The commenter does not state a relationship to Nolan, a firsthand basis, employer, dates, or supporting record. It is preserved as a low-confidence lead and must not be treated as verified swimming or employment history without corroboration.
A public news-style update stating that a body had been found and identity was not yet confirmed. Official and contemporaneous news records are stronger sources for the recovery chronology.

records.message: There were crowds and families who saw Nolan & said he was walking with a couple girls. He and his friends said ok, but they all agreed on a time to meet back at their boat. As soon as that time came and he was nowhere around, the friends contacted his mom & authorities Immediately! They were like brothers and are all devastated! Strong currants, riptides, undertows are no joke even if you’re an avid swimmer. And alcohol added to the mix is beyond risky. Takes a split second for something to happen and nobody have seen. One family in particular noticed him walking alone after walking around with the 2 girls. Him just looking at the water & boats. And the family was tending to their little kids or else they might have seen him possibly get in to cool off. This is all so terribly sad!
records.assessment: The writer does not identify the families, explain her basis, or provide exact times. The claim that family and authorities were contacted immediately conflicts with other public timing accounts. It is retained as a public-narrative lead, not a fact.

records.message: I feel like we seen him on the east end yesterday standing on one the sand dunes
records.assessment: The screenshot preserves tentative language and appears to describe the commenter’s own recollection of seeing Nolan on the east end on July 4. It supplies no exact time, position, image of Nolan, or independent confirmation.

records.message: Last time I spoke to him was when he said I have to leave and it was probably 2 to 2:30 but there was a huge group of people with several boats around for all I can remember. I last saw him get on a white boat with a center console before I had left so that’s all the information I can provide
records.status: Material lead; parent post and direct comment permalink unrecovered
records.assessment: The screenshot presents Lucas Aviz as describing his own conversation and sighting around 2:00–2:30 PM. The cropped parent post is unidentified, the direct Lucas comment was not recovered, and no vessel identity or native timestamp is authenticated. The white center-console boat must not be equated with MI4088BU.

records.message: last night as soon as they realized he hadn’t come back on another boat the coast guard was immediately notified as well as his parents. This kid is very good friends with the people he went out with. They are devastated and have been out there all morning/afternoon helping search for him too! ... And I know for a fact that the kid he went out with yesterday has been back out there all morning/afternoon with other buddies helping to search for him, along with their other friends in other boats...
records.assessment: The screenshot records a contemporaneous claim that friends returned to assist the search. It does not identify every person or establish the complete notification sequence, motives, or exact times.

records.message: to clarify: I never stated that I saw Nolan. I also never stated that the argument you hear on the video was directed to and/or involved Nolan. I simply posted this to see if he was spotted on camera after his last known sighting at 3pm as stated by law enforcement. *the reason this video was posted yesterday (7/6) is because like 98% of the attendees of Horn Island, I was very intoxicated. I did not even realize I had this video in my Snapchat until a friend who was also in attendance mentioned seeing this on my story and thought it would be helpful to the public when he was still labeled a missing person. This video was sent to the authorities and his mother before being posted. Please stop with the rumor mill. Let the investigators do their job.

additionalMedia.note: Archived only to document the misinformation Anna corrected; not evidence that Nolan appears or fought.
Five-second source video link; no autoplay.

records.status: Direct source for Anna’s own statements
records.assessment: This directly corrects the claim that Anna saw Nolan or said the argument involved him. It supports that she found the clip in Snapchat after a friend prompted her, sent it to authorities and Nolan’s mother, and posted it publicly on July 6. It still does not authenticate capture time, identify Nolan in the image, or establish the full sequence.

records.message: you can see me and my husband standing In the back of the boat in the video. The person yelling is someone in our boat (who was a mixed guy btw. Not that race matters but to a lot of people around this case it does. Also the guy yelling is also apart of the friend group Nolan was with and had been around them all day). But the guy was yelling because he got in a fight with a white guy and we broke it up and put him on our boat. He was pissed because he wanted to fight and we wouldn’t let him. 2 other white kids ended up fighting the original fight starter white guy. But The video is taken after the fight was already over. And DMR also showed up shortly after. Video was at 4:01 I remembered seeing a video on Anna’s story and told her to look through the footage. We saw someone resembling Nolan in the background. He was not involved in anyway with the actual altercation that happened. We were just trying to help with the timeline of things and possible documented sighting. Since it was originally stated he was last seen at 3 pm but video is at 4. We weren’t 100% it was him though. It could also help if it was him to identify who was potentially last with him.
records.status: Material direct reply; identity in video explicitly uncertain
records.assessment: Ivy identifies herself and her husband in the video and describes the altercation sequence from an apparent firsthand position. Her 4:01 time is not supported by native metadata in the public record, and she expressly says the person only resembled Nolan and that they were not 100% certain.

records.screenshotContext: The supplied screenshot shows Katelynn’s first statement, Briana May asking whether this was the group throwing beer cans and whether Nolan was with them, and Katelynn’s reply. A moving-caption overlay obscures a few words near the end, but the surrounding sentence reads as ‘having a good time.’ The screenshot appears to be a frame from an edited social video; the native parent-post permalink and native comment export have not been recovered.

records.grade: B-named firsthand account / derivative media preservation
records.status: Material firsthand account; native parent thread and media metadata remain unavailable
records.assessment: The two attributed statements form a coherent firsthand account: Katelynn says Nolan introduced himself to her husband, that her group was parked directly beside the group, and that Nolan was not in sight when her group left at 7:30 PM. This supports a no-sight observation in her immediate area at her departure time; it is not a case-wide last-sighting time and does not establish where Nolan was then. The statements do not say Katelynn witnessed Nolan refuse a ride. Her separate July 7 direct reply mentions another departure around 5 PM, but the pronouns and vessel remain unresolved. The public repost corroborates that the 7:30 statement circulated under her name while cropping out the follow-up reply; it does not authenticate the native comment or the attached scene images.

records.embeddedMessageTime: July 7 at 1:08 AM; year inferred as 2026 from case context and not displayed beside the message
messageContext: A displayed first-person statement alleges a dispute over Nolan’s phone, an argument continuing on shore, a physical confrontation involving several people, and a young woman asking them to stop.
The displayed speaker says her group left as the situation worsened and does not claim to know what happened after leaving.

A separate Instagram message screenshot marked July 7 at 1:08 AM says the sender was on another boat, witnessed an argument, intended to contact police, and says she and her husband had limited footage showing an argument.
The message uses future-tense language about going to police and submitting information. It does not establish that a law-enforcement agency received the account or footage.

Other attachments display an unavailable recipient profile and a statement defending the displayed account’s authenticity; neither independently proves identity, control, blocking, delivery, or police receipt.

records.status: Material reporting lead; identity, underlying allegations, footage, submission, and police receipt unverified
records.assessment: The public post and all five attachments are preserved. The embedded 1:08 AM message is evidence that the displayed sender expressed an intention to report information; future-tense wording does not show that police possessed it then or later. No direct Faith Lauren comment permalink was exposed during this review, and the post’s full comment tree was not audited.

records.captionExcerpt: reached out to me on 7/5/26 at around 11:30PM
records.captionContext: The poster identifies the screenshots as a conversation with Warren Hudson’s mother, Katie Hudson Seymour, concerning Warren, Nolan, Wyatt, and the Horn Island incident.

messageContext: The sender identifies herself as Warren’s mother, disputes the poster’s prior information, says Warren did not ride out or return with Nolan, and says Nolan was supposed to board Wyatt’s boat.
The sender says Wyatt repeatedly asked Nolan to get on the boat ‘at five when it was time to leave,’ but Nolan wanted to stay with a girl whose boat was parked next to Wyatt’s.
The sender says Wyatt asked several times within other people’s hearing, that Wyatt’s boat began filling with water, broke down, and was towed.
The sender says Warren was not on that boat, noticed Nolan was missing after returning to a friend’s house, and called Nolan’s mother, the Coast Guard, and the sheriff’s office.
The sender says she briefly saw Warren during a short trip with another son, had spent the day looking for Nolan, and repeatedly asks the poster to remove posts and family photographs.
The final visible recipient message asks whether the information and a description of the girl had been provided to law enforcement.

timelineClaim.claim: The sender says Wyatt repeatedly asked Nolan to board at five when it was time to leave, and that Nolan declined because he wanted to stay with a girl.
timelineClaim.conflict: MI4088BU’s official GPS summary records movement beginning at 4:31 PM; the screenshot’s five-o’clock wording is approximate, unauthenticated, and not reconciled to that record.

records.status: Material source lead; sender and claims not independently authenticated
records.assessment: The public post, caption context, four attachments, displayed conversation name, handle, and 11:26 PM interface marker are preserved. The screenshots establish what the post publicly attributed to the displayed sender. They do not independently authenticate the account holder, sender identity, phone ownership, complete conversation, message-date year, or truth and precision of the underlying claims. The five-o’clock wording is retained as a low-confidence secondhand timeline claim and does not override the verified 4:31 PM GPS movement.
